channel.title: Shi Pan — Blog
channel.description: Founding Researcher, PAVO AI · Research Fellow, Secrier Lab, UCL

item.title: Part 1: Can an Agent Own an Entire Simulation-Based Design Workflow?
item.description: Thirty runs across airfoil and battery simulations: the loop improved designs, but finding a feasible candidate did not mean selecting one. What would it take for an agent to own the evidence, not just the next parameter choice?

item.title: Can We Get Agents to Imitate the Steps by Which Humans Understand the World?
item.description: A formal model for agents that read papers, run experiments and evaluate candidates. The systematic gap I see is the ability to connect uncertainty, evidence-gathering costs, belief updates and action selection.

item.title: In 2026, Can I Just Talk to an Agent and Stop Opening Other Apps?
item.description: I did live through a single conversation interface, at the cost of becoming the system's operator. Making personal agents a consumer product requires harnesses to take integration, state management and recovery off the user's hands.

item.title: Can Classical Control Barrier Functions Measure Agent Safety?
item.description: Using control barrier functions to describe an agent's margin before a constraint violation. A safety guarantee must come with its abstraction errors, environmental assumptions and adversary model—not just its final inequality.

item.title: What Should Lifelong Learning Really Be About?
item.description: A framework combining environmental change, limited capacity and knowledge an agent cannot afford to lose. Lifelong learning should ask not only whether an agent forgets, but how long it can remain able to act in an uncertain world.

item.title: Can Agents Run Uber?
item.description: An agent team runs a simulated ride-hailing company on one budget. One run ends in bankruptcy after 138 ticks: writing code is not the same as running a business, where timing, feedback and intervention costs matter.

item.title: Can We Build an LLM Evaluation Table That Never Saturates?
item.description: Evaluating nine models from three families through 27 cognitive operators. The aim is a capability score with no preset ceiling, rather than another percentage-based report card.

item.title: How Task Partitioning and Communication Limit Multi-Agent Collaboration
item.description: Task partitioning can leave information gaps that internal communication cannot overcome in a closed system. Collaboration design should start with dependencies that must stay intact and the new information execution can provide.

item.title: How far are we from automating the whole training run?
item.description: A map of pretraining and post-training as concrete work steps, tracing how models help produce their successors. My view: within industrial workflows that retain the technical approach, recursive self-improvement is approaching its final leap.

item.title: Do Silicon Samples Dream of Electric Sheep?
item.description: Does copying a person's behavioural data into a model let us simulate that person? A literature map separating the reproduction of past answers from learning the patterns that generate behaviour.
